featured_reviews.review_text:
An Experience to Share

I and my brother are persons with 96% disability and wheelchair-bound. My brother had skin-related issues, and since this clinic was nearby, we contacted them. The doctor agreed to give the first consultation online via video call/WhatsApp, as we request the clinic as it is not wheelchair accessible and it’s difficult for us to sit on regular chairs.

After 5 days of treatment, the doctor had advised us to follow up if the infection persisted. When we reached out again, the infection was less but new rashes had started. At that point, the clinic asked us to visit physically, which was not possible due to the lack of wheelchair accessibility. We requested a home visit, explaining our situation as persons with disabilities, but were informed that the doctor does not do home visits.

We completely understand infrastructure limitations. However, what was truly disheartening was the lack of consideration or willingness to make an exception for a disabled patient — especially when our home is barely 10 minutes away by walk or just a few minutes by auto/bike. If the doctor agreed, our parents were ready to personally pick and drop them.

Even after completing the 10-day course of treatment, when my brother again contacted the clinic to share progress, ongoing problems, and asked if consultation could be continued online with photos/WhatsApp (as visiting is not possible), the message was simply ignored. It has now been 4 days without any response. We don’t know if the message was not delivered, or if we have been blocked, but the silence itself is very concerning.

It was really upsetting that despite knowing our condition, the clinic’s only solution was to insist on a physical visit to a place that itself is not disability-friendly. Such an approach, particularly from a medical professional, feels disappointing and discouraging for patients like us.
